newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy minister sees new managers for railway.
newsitem.headline: Italy minister sees new managers for railway.

text.p: Italy's state railway is likely to undergo a change of management following the arrest of its chief executive Lorenzo Necci in a corruption probe, Industry Minister Pier Luigi Bersani said on Wednesday.
He told reporters that a change at the top of Ferrovie dello Stato, where managing director Necci was planning a huge high-speed rail project, was "pretty likely".

"The government seeks to respond to problems promptly," Basanini said when asked whether comments by Prime Minister Romano Prodi on the need to renew the managers of state companies also applied to the railways.
"The government intends to guarantee that the operations of the infrastructure system go ahead," he said.

Necci, one of Italy's most prominent public sector executives, was arrested in the northwest town of La Spezia on Sunday on suspicion of crimes including fraud, embezzlement, false accounting, corruption and abuse of office.
The snowballing investigation has sparked reminders of the "Tangentopoli" (Bribesville) graft scandal of the 1990s that toppled Italy's corrupt political old guard.
Italian television said magistrates were investigating up to 50 people in the probe. The head of an arms firm and two magistrates were among five people arrested on Tuesday.
